legacy.access_ip_error: Could not save the IP list.
legacy.access_ip_invalid: Enter one private IPv4 or unique-local IPv6 address.
legacy.access_load_error: The saved IP list could not be read. Password sign-in still works; adding a valid IP replaces the damaged list.
legacy.access_password_invalid: Passwords must match and the new password must be 12–128 characters.
legacy.alerts_error: Could not save the login alert settings.
legacy.alerts_intro: Push logins from new addresses and failed-login bans to your phone through Bark. The key is the last part of the push URL in the Bark app.
legacy.alerts_invalid: The server must start with https:// or http://; the key may contain only letters, digits, - and _.
legacy.alerts_load_error: The login alert settings file is invalid; alerts are treated as not set up.
legacy.alerts_on_ban: Alert when a ban is triggered
legacy.alerts_on_new_ip: Alert on login from a new address
legacy.alerts_status_off: No push key; no alerts are sent.
legacy.alerts_test_failed: The test alert failed. Check the server address, the key and the host's network.
legacy.alerts_test_sent: Test alert sent; check your phone.
legacy.audit_intro: The latest 50 logins and security setting changes, kept on the server (up to 500).
legacy.client_cert_autoselect: Stop picking the certificate every time
legacy.client_cert_autoselect_help: Download the file for this device's system and run it; from then on the browser picks this certificate for the console without asking.
legacy.client_cert_current_none: This connection did not present a certificate.
legacy.client_cert_current_none_hint: No certificate on this device yet? Each device uses its own: enter a device name below to generate one; the page that follows has one-click setup files. If you already imported one and still see this, the browser was most likely not fully restarted.
legacy.client_cert_error: The certificate operation failed; the certificate files may not be writable.
legacy.client_cert_intro: Log in with a certificate instead of, or together with, the password: generate a certificate for each device, import it into the system or browser, and the browser presents it when the console opens. Choose the login method below; with "Certificate only" or "Password + certificate", a device without a certificate cannot even open the login page.
legacy.client_cert_issued_text: Note the import password. It is shown only once and the server keeps no private key; after leaving this page you can only generate a new one.
legacy.client_cert_keep_current: While certificates are required, the certificate this connection uses cannot be revoked.
legacy.client_cert_manual: Manual import (Android, iOS, Firefox, or if the one-click setup fails)
legacy.client_cert_name_invalid: The device name must be 1 to 40 characters.
legacy.client_cert_need_current: Import a certificate and reopen the console with it (this page then shows the certificate in use) before turning this on, so you cannot lock yourself out.
legacy.client_cert_openssl_missing: The bundled openssl is missing, so certificates cannot be generated. Running the installer again restores it.
legacy.client_cert_os_android: Android: Settings > Security > Encryption & credentials > Install a certificate > VPN & app user certificate, then pick the file.
legacy.client_cert_os_firefox: Firefox does not use the system store by default: import it separately under Settings > Privacy & Security > Certificates > View Certificates > Your Certificates.
legacy.client_cert_os_ios: iOS / iPadOS: open it in Files, then install it under Settings > Profile Downloaded.
legacy.client_cert_os_macos: macOS: double-click the file and add it to the login keychain.
legacy.client_cert_os_windows: Windows: double-click the file, choose Current User as the store location and Personal as the store (or let the wizard choose).
legacy.client_cert_required_text: This console only accepts devices with an imported client certificate. Import one, then fully quit and reopen the browser. If the certificate is lost, follow the README to restore password login as root on the server.
legacy.client_cert_setup_linux: Run it in a terminal with bash
legacy.client_cert_setup_macos: Double-click, then install it in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Profiles
legacy.client_cert_step_download: Download the certificate file. Downloading alone is not enough: browsers do not read certificates from the Downloads folder.
legacy.client_cert_step_import: Import it into the system certificate store, entering the import password above:
legacy.client_cert_step_restart: Fully quit and reopen the browser. Closing the window is not enough: Chrome and Edge may keep running in the background. Open chrome://restart or edge://restart, or quit from the system tray.
legacy.client_cert_step_setup: Download the one-click setup file for this device's system and run it, entering the import password above when asked. It imports the certificate and makes Chrome and Edge pick it on their own from now on.
legacy.client_cert_step_verify: Reopen the console's security settings. Once the certificate in use is shown, turn on Require client certificate. If the browser asks for a certificate, pick this one.
legacy.client_cert_steps_title: Next, complete these three steps in order
legacy.client_cert_tls_unsupported: This host's TLS library cannot verify client certificates (self test failed), so certificates are disabled. Update the system openssl/libssl packages, then generate a certificate again.
legacy.console_access_error: Could not save the console access list.
legacy.console_access_intro: When on, only listed addresses can connect to the console; others are dropped before the TLS handshake and never see the login page. Loopback is always allowed. LAN devices, Clash subscriptions included, must be listed too.
legacy.console_access_invalid: Enter a single IP address or a CIDR network.
legacy.console_access_keep_current: Removing this would lock out the current connection. Turn the limit off or add another entry that covers it first.
legacy.console_access_load_error: The console access list file is invalid; the limit is treated as off.
legacy.console_access_need_current: Add the current address first, or turning this on would lock you out.
legacy.console_access_recovery: If you are locked out, run this as root on the server to turn the limit off; no restart needed:
legacy.console_access_too_wide: A network covering every address cannot be added.
legacy.login_ban_cleared: Failed login records and bans cleared.
legacy.login_ban_disabled: Failed login ban turned off. Failures are still recorded.
legacy.login_ban_empty: No failed logins since the web console started.
legacy.login_ban_error: Could not save the failed login ban setting.
legacy.login_ban_load_error: The failed login ban settings file is invalid; the ban is treated as on.
legacy.login_ban_observe_hint: When off, failures are still counted and a threshold hit is flagged instead of banned, so you can test detection. Switching clears current bans and flags.
legacy.login_ban_rule: After {count} wrong passwords from one IP (IPv6 grouped by /64) within {window}s, it is banned: {first} the first time, ten times longer for each repeat within a day, at most {max}. A successful login clears its count.
legacy.login_ban_switch: Ban IPs with too many failures
legacy.login_global_flagged: Global threshold reached, not paused ({seconds}s left).
legacy.login_global_rule: When all sources together get {count} wrong passwords within {window}s, password login pauses for {duration} for addresses that never logged in successfully.
legacy.login_mode_both_help: The device must present a valid certificate and the password must be entered; one alone is not enough.
legacy.login_mode_cert_help: Only a client certificate logs in; a device without one reaches nothing. The terminal and security settings still ask for the password.
legacy.login_mode_either_help: Either the password or a certificate logs in.
legacy.login_mode_hint: Before switching to "Certificate only" or "Password + certificate", open this page with an active certificate (the one in use is shown above), or you lock yourself out. If you lose the certificate, run `python3 /root/apps/vps-server/src/web/client_cert.py disable` on the server to go back to password only.
legacy.login_mode_password_help: Only the password logs in; a certificate the browser sends is ignored.
legacy.module_held_by_domains: Ports 80 and 443 are used by domain forwarding or the IP certificate
legacy.module_public_needs_ipcert: HTTPS needs the IP certificate on
legacy.module_source_missing: Installer files are unavailable. Upgrade from a complete checkout first.
legacy.module_tailscale_asset_missing: The bundled Tailscale archive is missing. Rerun deploy/install.sh from complete source or an offline Release bundle containing the third_party/tailscale archive, extracted into a separate directory, while preserving the existing installation and state directories, then retry.
legacy.module_uninstall_confirm: Uninstall {name}? Its configuration and nodes are kept and backed up on the server, and restored when you install it again.
legacy.sessions_intro: A login lasts at most {ttl} and ends after {idle} without activity.
legacy.sessions_revoked: The selected devices were signed out.
legacy.sessions_use_logout: Use Log out for this device.
legacy.total_actual_gib: Usage the provider shows for this period (GiB)
legacy.total_calibrate_hint: The count can differ from what the provider bills. Enter the usage shown in the provider's panel for this period; the console stores the difference as a "calibration", shows it as its own bar above and includes it in the total; it clears itself when the next period begins. Leave it empty and save to clear the calibration.
legacy.total_hint: Adds up nodes, FRPS, domain forwarding, port forwarding, FRPC, Tailscale, iperf3, Mini Drive and speed test, counted as on their own pages (forwarded traffic ×2). The reset happens at 00:00 UTC; console pages, the terminal and SSH are not counted.
legacy.total_multiplier_note: Each figure is billed usage: nodes, FRPS and forwarding count every byte twice (in and out), so it is double what that feature's own page shows. The period runs from the reset day and includes what each source has already used in its current cycle.
legacy.total_over: The total traffic limit is reached. This only warns for now; nothing is throttled or cut off.
legacy.total_warn: More than 80% of the total traffic limit is used.
